chief_complaint: neck pain radiating down lateral arm into thumb and index finger with weak biceps/wrist extension and diminished brachioradialis reflex
hpi_details: 48M presenting with C6 dermatomal pain, positive Spurling compression test, 4/5 wrist extension weakness, and diminished 1+ brachioradialis reflex where cervical spine MRI confirms C5-C6 foraminal stenosis responding to cervical traction physical therapy and oral steroids.
ideas: He thinks he severely pinched a nerve in his neck after falling asleep in an awkward position on the sofa.
concerns: He is worried that the weakness in his hand will become permanent and prevent him from safely gripping steering wheels and tools.
expectations: He hopes to receive a strong anti-inflammatory treatment and a referral for physical therapy so he can regain his grip strength.

available_results.value: C5-C6 right foraminal disc-osteophyte complex causing severe right neural foraminal stenosis and C6 nerve-root impingement; no cord compression

Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to peripheral entrapment neuropathy without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

red_flags: Progressive arm weakness or loss of hand function
Gait imbalance or bowel/bladder dysfunction suggesting cervical myelopathy

must_ask.say: Does the neck pain travel into your shoulder, arm, thumb, or index finger?
Does turning or extending your neck make the arm pain or tingling worse?
Have you developed hand clumsiness, trouble walking, or bowel or bladder changes?
Does looking up or turning your head toward the painful side reproduce the arm symptoms?
Have you noticed weakness when lifting, bending your elbow, extending your wrist, or gripping?

history.answer: My neck has been hurting, and a sharp pain shoots down my right arm into my thumb and index finger, and my arm feels weak.
It is both numbness and weakness. I have a numb, tingling pain shooting down my arm, and my wrist and arm feel weaker when I try to lift things.
The pain is only on my right side. It starts in my neck and travels down the outside of my arm right into my thumb and index finger.
It started about two weeks ago over a few days, initially as an ache that progressively turned into sharp shooting pains.
It has gradually become more intense over the past two weeks, and the weakness became noticeable a few days ago.
I have trouble holding a heavy coffee mug or typing for long periods because my wrist tires easily, but buttoning my shirt and walking are fine.
Looking up or turning my head to the right makes the pain shoot down my arm immediately. Resting my neck or supporting my arm slightly eases it.
Yes, I have an aching stiffness in the right side of my neck that fires like an electric shock down to my hand. My lower back feels totally fine.
No, I haven't had any facial drooping, slurred speech, double vision, dizziness, or difficulty swallowing.
No, my bowel and bladder habits are completely normal, and I have no numbness around my groin.
My legs feel strong and normal. I have no trouble walking, no clumsiness in my feet, and no electric shock sensations down my spine.
No, I don't have any shortness of breath, drooping eyelids, double vision, or trouble chewing or swallowing.
No, I have not noticed any muscle twitching or visible shrinking in my arm muscles.
No, I haven't had a cold, fever, cough, or stomach flu recently.
I take medication for high blood pressure and have mildly elevated cholesterol, but I don't have diabetes or heart rhythm issues.
I eat a regular balanced diet with plenty of meat and vegetables, and I have never had any stomach or bowel surgery.
No, I do not take water pills, steroids, or chemotherapy drugs.
I do some computer work, but I don't do heavy repetitive wrist work, and leaning on my elbow or bending my wrist doesn't trigger the pain.
I notice the weakness mainly when bending my elbow against resistance or trying to pull my hand back at the wrist.
Whenever I tilt my head back and turn toward the right, or if pressure is applied to my neck, that exact sharp pain shoots into my thumb.
It travels from my right neck, over the collarbone, down the outside of my upper arm and forearm, and directly into my thumb and index finger.
I figured I must have pinched a nerve in my neck pretty badly from falling asleep in a weird position on the sofa last weekend.
I'm worried that this weakness in my right wrist is permanent and that I won't be able to safely hold a steering wheel or use tools around the house.
I'm hoping for a strong painkiller or anti-inflammatory shot today, along with physical therapy to help get the strength back in my hand.
I have high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol, both diagnosed a couple of years ago.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I take Lisinopril 10 milligrams once every morning, and I don't take any regular supplements or over-the-counter pain pills.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe one or two glasses of wine or beer on the weekend.
I work as an office administrator, lead an active lifestyle, and live at home with my wife and children.
My father has high blood pressure, and my mother is doing well. There is no family history of nerve disorders or stroke.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7 °C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, well-appearing adult male in mild discomfort, holding his neck slightly stiffly.
Tenderness over the right lower cervical paraspinal musculature; Spurling test reproduces sharp shooting pain radiating down the right lateral arm into the thumb; no midline vertebral tenderness.
Right wrist extension strength 4/5 and right elbow flexion 4/5; right triceps, hand intrinsics, left upper extremity, and bilateral lower extremities are 5/5.
Decreased light touch and pinprick sensation over the right lateral forearm, thumb, and index finger; sensation is intact in all other dermatomes.

Right brachioradialis reflex is diminished at 1+; right biceps reflex 1+; right triceps reflex 2+; left upper extremity and bilateral lower extremity reflexes are 2+; Babinski sign is negative bilaterally.
Right shoulder shows full active and passive range of motion without impingement; Phalen and Tinel tests at both wrists and elbows are negative.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact with symmetric facial movements, clear speech, and normal extraocular motion.
Normal casual and tandem gait without ataxia; Romberg test is negative.
